ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $ \angle AOB=30^\circ$, P is a point on the bisector of $\angle AOB$, $PM \perp OB$ at point M, $PN \parallel OB$ intersects OA at point N, if PM=1, what is the length of PN?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw $PD\perp AO$ at point D, \\
since P lies on the angle bisector of $\angle AOB$ and $PM\perp OB$ at point M, \\
therefore $\angle AOP=\angle BOP=15^\circ$, and $PD=PM=1$, \\
since $PN\parallel OB$, \\
therefore $\angle NPO=\angle BOP=15^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle DNP=30^\circ$, \\
hence $PN=2PD=\boxed{2}$.
ready1_open_rewrite.title: MM-Math open-ended problem
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, \(\angle AOB = 30^\circ\). Point \(P\) is on the bisector of \(\angle AOB\). \(PM \perp OB\) at \(M\), and \(PN \parallel OB\) intersects \(OA\) at \(N\). If \(PM = 1\), what is the length of \(PN\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: Draw \(PD \perp AO\) at point \(D\). Since \(P\) lies on the angle bisector of \(\angle AOB\) and \(PM \perp OB\), we have \(\angle AOP = \angle BOP = 15^\circ\), and \(PD = PM = 1\). Since \(PN \parallel OB\), \(\angle NPO = \angle BOP = 15^\circ\). Thus \(\angle DNP = 30^\circ\), hence \(PN = 2PD = 2\).

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, point O is at the lower left, ray OB goes horizontally to the right from O, and ray OA goes obliquely to the upper right from O, forming ∠AOB. Point P is located on an oblique line inside the angle; from P, a perpendicular is drawn downward to OB, with foot M, and there is a right-angle mark at M in the figure. Through P there is a line segment PN parallel to OB, which extends leftward and intersects OA at N. Reasoning: Because PM ⟂ OB and PM = 1, and PN ∥ OB, the perpendicular distance from point P to line OB is the distance between the two parallel lines PN and OB, which is 1. Since N is also on line PN, the perpendicular distance from N to OB is likewise 1. Draw a perpendicular from N to OB; then in the right triangle with ON as the hypotenuse, ON lies along OA, and ∠AOB = 30°, so this perpendicular distance equals ON·sin30°. Therefore ON·sin30° = 1, obtaining ON·1/2 = 1, hence ON = 2. Also because P is on the angle bisector of ∠AOB, ∠PON = 15°. At the same time PN ∥ OB, so ∠OPN equals the angle between OP and OB, also 15°. Thus in triangle OPN, ∠PON = ∠OPN, so their opposite sides are equal, namely PN = ON = 2.
